names: Grandson of the Marquis of Yingyin

cause.en: refused to face judicial interrogation after losing the way
charged with encroaching on Emperor Jing's park land

value.qualitative: Home retirement period before hunting with Pingye in Blue Hills per s0060–s0061.
value.event: Grandson of the Marquis of Yingyin hunted during home retirement years anchored at s0060.

value.qualitative: Same home-retirement window as s0060; Baling post encounter follows hunting per s0063.
value.event: Baling Commandant incident occurs within the home-retirement period named at s0060.

units.zh: 李將軍廣者，隴西成紀人也。
units.en: General Li Guang was a native of Chengji in Longxi.
units.literal: General Li Guang, Longxi Chengji person.

units.zh: 其先曰李信，秦時為將，逐得燕太子丹者也。
units.en: His ancestor Li Xin had served as a general under the Qin and was the man who pursued and captured Dan, the Crown Prince of Yan.
units.literal: His ancestor named Li Xin, Qin time became general, pursued captured Yan crown prince Dan.

units.zh: 故槐裏，徙成紀。
units.en: The family was originally from Huaili but later moved to Chengji.
units.literal: Originally Huaili, moved to Chengji.

units.zh: 廣家世世受射。
units.en: For generations, the Li family had handed down the art of archery.
units.literal: Guang family generation generation received archery.

units.zh: 孝文帝十四年，匈奴大入蕭關，而廣以良家子從軍擊胡，用善騎射，殺首虜多，為漢中郎。
units.en: In the fourteenth year of Emperor Wen's reign, the Xiongnu launched a major invasion through the Xiao Pass. Guang, as the son of a respectable family, joined the army to fight the barbarians. His skill in horsemanship and archery allowed him to kill a great many of the enemy, and he was appointed as an Attendant at the Han court.
units.literal: Emperor Wen fourteenth year, Xiongnu greatly entered Xiaoguan, and Guang with good family son followed army attacked Hu, used good horsemanship archery, killed enemy leaders many, became Han imperial attendant.

units.zh: 廣從弟李蔡亦為郎，皆為武騎常侍，秩八百石。
units.en: Guang's younger cousin Li Cai also served as an Attendant. Both were appointed as Regular Attendants of the Martial Cavalry, with a salary rank of eight hundred shi.
units.literal: Guang younger cousin Li Cai also became imperial attendant, all became martial cavalry regular attendants, rank eight hundred shi.

units.zh: 嘗從行，有所衝陷折關及格猛獸，而文帝曰：「惜乎，子不遇時！
units.en: Once, while accompanying the Emperor on campaign, Guang charged through barriers and grappled with fierce beasts, and Emperor Wen said, "What a pity that you were not born in your season!
units.literal: Once on campaign in attendance, there were charges through barriers and grappling with fierce beasts, and Emperor Wen said, "What a pity—you were not born in your season!

units.zh: 如令子當高帝時，萬戶侯豈足道哉！」
units.en: Had you lived in the age of Emperor Gao, a marquisate of ten thousand households would scarcely be worth mentioning!"
units.literal: If you had been in the time of Emperor Gao, would a marquis of ten thousand households not be spoken of with ease!"

units.zh: 及孝景初立，廣為隴西都尉，徙為騎郎將。
units.en: When Emperor Jing first ascended the throne, Guang was appointed Commandant of Longxi and later transferred to the post of Captain of the Cavalry.
units.literal: When Emperor Jing initially established, Guang became Longxi commandery governor, moved became cavalry captain.

units.zh: 吳楚軍時，廣為驍騎都尉，從太尉亞夫擊吳楚軍，取旗，顯功名昌邑下。
units.en: During the Rebellion of Wu and Chu, Guang served as Commandant of the Brave Cavalry. He followed Grand Commandant Zhou Yafu in the attack against the rebel armies, captured an enemy battle standard, and won renown at the walls of Changyi.
units.literal: Wu-Chu army time, Guang became brave-cavalry commandant, followed Grand Commandant Yafu attacking Wu-Chu armies, took a flag, and displayed merit and fame below Changyi.

units.zh: 以梁王授廣將軍印，還，賞不行。
units.en: But because the King of Liang had bestowed upon him a general's seal, he received no reward from the court upon his return.
units.literal: Because Liang wang gave Guang general seal, return, reward not carried out.

units.zh: 徙為上谷太守，匈奴日以合戰。
units.en: He was transferred to serve as Governor of Shanggu, where he fought the Xiongnu in battle day after day.
units.literal: Moved became Shanggu governor, Xiongnu daily with engage battle.

units.zh: 典屬國公孫昆邪為上泣曰：「李廣才氣，天下無雙，自負其能，數與虜敵戰，恐亡之。」
units.en: Gongsun Kunye, Director of Attendants for Dependent States, wept before the emperor and said, "General Li Guang's talent and spirit are unmatched under Heaven. He is so confident in his own ability that he repeatedly engages the enemy in battle, and I fear we shall lose him."
units.literal: Gongsun Kunye, Director of Attendants for Dependent States, wept before the emperor and said, "General Li Guang's talent and spirit are unmatched in the realm. Trusting in his ability, he repeatedly fights the enemy in person—I fear we shall lose him."

units.zh: 於是乃徙為上郡太守。
units.en: He was thereupon transferred to serve as Governor of Shangjun.
units.literal: Thereupon then moved became Shangjun governor.

units.zh: 後廣轉為邊郡太守，徙上郡。
units.en: Later Guang was rotated through the border commanderies, and was transferred to Shangjun.
units.literal: Later Guang transferred became border commandery governor, moved Shangjun.

units.zh: 嘗為隴西、北地、鴈門、代郡、雲中太守，皆以力戰為名。
units.en: At one time or another he served as Governor of Longxi, Beidi, Yanmen, Dai, and Yunzhong, winning fame at each post through fierce combat.
units.literal: Once became Longxi, Beidi, Yanmen, Daijun, Yunzhong governors, all with vigorous battle for fame.

units.zh: 匈奴大入上郡，天子使中貴人從廣勒習兵擊匈奴。
units.en: When the Xiongnu launched a major invasion into Shangjun, the Emperor sent a palace eunuch to join Guang in drilling the troops and leading the attack against the Xiongnu.
units.literal: Xiongnu greatly entered Shangjun, emperor sent palace favorite followed Guang drilled practiced troops attacked Xiongnu.

units.zh: 中貴人將騎數十縱，見匈奴三人，與戰。
units.en: The eunuch, leading several dozen riders on a foray, encountered three Xiongnu horsemen and engaged them in combat.
units.literal: Palace favorite led cavalry several ten released, saw Xiongnu three people, with battle.

units.zh: 三人還射，傷中貴人，殺其騎且盡。
units.en: The three men wheeled around and shot back, wounding the eunuch and killing nearly all of his cavalry.
units.literal: Three people returned shot, injured palace favorite, killed his cavalry almost all.

units.zh: 中貴人走廣。
units.en: The eunuch fled back to Guang.
units.literal: Palace favorite fled to Guang.

units.zh: 廣曰：「是必射雕者也。」
units.en: Guang said, "Those must be eagle hunters."
units.literal: Guang said, "Those must be eagle-shooters."

units.zh: 廣乃遂從百騎往馳三人。
units.en: Guang thereupon took a hundred horsemen and rode out in pursuit of the three men.
units.literal: Guang then from hundred cavalry went galloped pursue three people.

units.zh: 三人亡馬步行，行數十里。
units.en: The three men had lost their horses and were traveling on foot. After Guang had chased them for a few dozen li,
units.literal: The three men had lost their horses and were traveling on foot; they had gone several tens of li.

units.zh: 廣令其騎張左右翼，而廣身自射彼三人者，殺其二人，生得一人，果匈奴射雕者也。
units.en: Guang ordered his horsemen to fan out to the left and right while he himself shot at the three men, killing two and taking one alive. They were indeed Xiongnu eagle shooters.
units.literal: Guang ordered his cavalry spread left right wings, and Guang personally shot those three people, killed their two people, alive captured one person, indeed Xiongnu shooting eagle ones.

units.zh: 已縛之上馬，望匈奴有數千騎，見廣，以為誘騎，皆驚，上山陳。
units.en: After they had bound the prisoner and mounted their horses, they spotted several thousand Xiongnu cavalry in the distance. The Xiongnu saw Guang's men and, taking them for a decoy force, were alarmed and drew up in battle formation on the hillside.
units.literal: Already bound placed on horse, looked Xiongnu had several thousand cavalry, saw Guang, considered lure cavalry, all alarmed, ascended mountain arrayed.

units.zh: 廣之百騎皆大恐，欲馳還走。
units.en: Guang's hundred horsemen were seized with terror and wanted to gallop back to safety.
units.literal: Guang his hundred cavalry all greatly feared, wanted gallop return flee.

units.zh: 廣曰：「吾去大軍數十里，今如此以百騎走，匈奴追射我立盡。
units.en: Guang said, "We are dozens of li from the main army. If we now flee with only a hundred horsemen like this, the Xiongnu will pursue and shoot us down to the last man.
units.literal: Guang said, "We are several tens of li from the main army. If we now flee with only a hundred horsemen like this, the Xiongnu will pursue and shoot us down to the last man.

units.zh: 今我留，匈奴必以我為大軍［之］誘（之），必不敢擊我。」
units.en: If we remain here, the Xiongnu will surely think we are a decoy for the main army and will not dare attack us."
units.literal: If we stay now, the Xiongnu are sure to take us for a decoy force of the main army and will not dare attack us."

units.zh: 廣令諸騎曰：「前！」
units.en: Guang ordered his men, saying, "Forward!"
units.literal: Guang ordered the horsemen, saying, "Forward!"

units.zh: 前未到匈奴陳二里所，止，令曰：「皆下馬解鞍！」
units.en: They advanced until they were only about two li from the Xiongnu formation, then halted, and Guang ordered, "All of you, dismount and loosen your saddles!"
units.literal: They advanced to within about two li of the Xiongnu battle line, halted, and he ordered, "All dismount and loosen your saddles!"

units.zh: 其騎曰：「虜多且近，即有急，柰何？」
units.en: His horsemen said, "The enemy are numerous and close. If something urgent happens, what will we do?"
units.literal: His horsemen said, "The enemy are many and near; if there is an emergency, what then?"

units.zh: 廣曰：「彼虜以我為走，今皆解鞍以示不走，用堅其意。」
units.en: Guang said, "Those barbarians think we are men about to run. If we all loosen our saddles now, we show that we will not flee, and so make them more certain of what they believe."
units.literal: Guang said, "Those barbarians take us for men who would flee. By loosening our saddles now we show that we do not flee, to strengthen their belief."

units.zh: 於是胡騎遂不敢擊。
units.en: And so the barbarian cavalry did not dare to attack.
units.literal: Thereupon Hu cavalry then not dared attack.

units.zh: 有白馬將出護其兵，李廣上馬與十餘騎奔射殺胡白馬將，而復還至其騎中，解鞍，令士皆縱馬臥。
units.en: A barbarian general on a white horse rode out to marshal his troops. Li Guang mounted up and, with a dozen or so riders, galloped forward and shot the white-horse general dead. He then returned to his own men, unsaddled the horses, and ordered the soldiers to release the horses and lie down.
units.literal: Had white horse general out protected their troops, Li Guang mounted horse with ten remainder cavalry galloped shot killed Hu white horse general, and again returned to his cavalry middle, loosened saddles, ordered soldiers all released horses lay down.

units.zh: 是時會暮，胡兵終怪之，不敢擊。
units.en: By then dusk had fallen. The barbarian troops, deeply suspicious, still did not dare to attack.
units.literal: At time met dusk, Hu troops finally wondered it, not dared attack.

units.zh: 夜半時，胡兵亦以為漢有伏軍於旁欲夜取之，胡皆引兵而去。
units.en: At midnight, the barbarian troops, now convinced that the Han had an ambush force hidden nearby waiting to strike under cover of darkness, withdrew their forces and departed.
units.literal: Midnight time, Hu troops also considered Han had ambush army at side wanted night take them, Hu all led troops left.

units.zh: 平旦，李廣乃歸其大軍。
units.en: At dawn, Li Guang led his men back to the main army.
units.literal: Dawn, Li Guang then returned his main army.

units.zh: 大軍不知廣所之，故弗從。
units.en: The main army, not knowing where Guang had gone, had been unable to provide support.
units.literal: Main army not knew Guang where went, therefore not followed.

units.zh: 居久之，孝景崩，武帝立，左右以為廣名將也，於是廣以上郡太守為未央衛尉，而程不識亦為長樂衛尉。
units.en: Some time later, Emperor Jing passed away, and Emperor Wu ascended the throne. The Emperor's advisors considered Guang a renowned general, and so he was transferred from his post as Governor of Shangjun to become Commander of the Weiyang Palace Guard, while Cheng Bushi was made Commander of the Changle Palace Guard.
units.literal: Resided long time, Emperor Jing passed, Emperor Wu established, attendants considered Guang famous general, thereupon Guang with Shangjun governor became Weiyang guard wei, and Cheng Bushi also became Changle guard wei.

units.zh: 程不識故與李廣俱以邊太守將軍屯。
units.en: Cheng Bushi had formerly served alongside Li Guang as a border governor and garrison commander.
units.literal: Cheng Bushi originally with Li Guang both as border governors generals garrisoned.

units.zh: 及出擊胡，而廣行無部伍行陳，就善水草屯，舍止，人人自便，不擊刀鬬以自衛，莫府省約文書籍事，然亦遠斥候，未嘗遇害。
units.en: When they marched out to fight the barbarians, Guang imposed no formal ranks or battle formations. He camped wherever there was good water and grass, and let each man see to his own needs. He did not use sentries beating watch clappers for defense, and his headquarters kept its paperwork to a minimum. Yet he always sent scouts far afield and was never taken by surprise.
units.literal: When out attacked Hu, and Guang marched without divisions rows arrayed, approached good water grass garrisoned, resided stopped, people each self convenient, not beat drums fought to self defend, headquarters office reduced simplified documents books matters, but also far sent scouts, never encountered harm.

units.zh: 程不識正部曲行伍營陳，擊刀鬬，士吏治軍簿至明，軍不得休息，然亦未嘗遇害。
units.en: Cheng Bushi, by contrast, maintained strict formations and encampments, posted sentries with watch clappers, and kept his officers working on military records until dawn. His troops got little rest, but he too was never taken by surprise.
units.literal: Cheng Bushi corrected divisions rows arrayed garrisoned, beat drums fought, officers officials managed army registers to dawn, army not got rest, but also never encountered harm.

units.zh: 不識曰：「李廣軍極簡易，然虜卒犯之，無以禁也；
units.en: Cheng Bushi said, "General Li Guang’s army is exceedingly loose and simple; if the enemy suddenly falls upon it, there is no way to restrain them.
units.literal: Cheng Bushi said, "General Li Guang's army is extremely lax, yet if the enemy suddenly attacks it, there is no way to stop them;

units.zh: 而其士卒亦佚樂，咸樂為之死。
units.en: Yet his soldiers lived at their ease and were content, and every one of them would gladly have died for him.
units.literal: And his soldiers also relaxed happy, all happy for him die.

units.zh: 我軍雖煩擾，然虜亦不得犯我。」
units.en: My army may be burdensome and exacting, but the enemy cannot break into it."
units.literal: My army is troublesome and exacting, yet the enemy also cannot break through us."

units.zh: 是時漢邊郡李廣、程不識皆為名將，然匈奴畏李廣之略，士卒亦多樂從李廣而苦程不識。
units.en: At that time, Li Guang and Cheng Bushi were both renowned generals of the Han border commanderies. But the Xiongnu feared Li Guang's cunning, and the soldiers too preferred to serve under Li Guang, finding service under Cheng Bushi a hardship.
units.literal: At time Han border commanderies Li Guang, Cheng Bushi all were famous generals, but Xiongnu feared Li Guang strategy, soldiers also many happy followed Li Guang but suffered Cheng Bushi.

units.zh: 程不識孝景時以數直諫為太中大夫。
units.en: During the reign of Emperor Jing, Cheng Bushi had been appointed Grand Palace Master for his repeated candid remonstrances.
units.literal: Cheng Bushi Emperor Jing time with repeatedly straight advised became palace grand master.

units.zh: 為人廉，謹於文法。
units.en: He was a man of integrity who was scrupulous in his adherence to regulations.
units.literal: As person incorrupt, careful with written law.

units.zh: 後漢以馬邑城誘單于，使大軍伏馬邑旁谷，而廣為驍騎將軍，領屬護軍將軍。
units.en: Later, the Han used the city of Mayi to lure the Chanyu into a trap, stationing the main army in ambush in the valleys around Mayi. Guang served as the General of the Brave Cavalry, under the command of the General of the Guard.
units.literal: Later Han with Maiyi city lured chanyu, sent main army ambushed Maiyi side valley, and Guang became fierce cavalry general, led belonged protect army general.

units.zh: 是時單于覺之，去，漢軍皆無功。
units.en: But the Chanyu discovered the trap and withdrew, and the Han army accomplished nothing.
units.literal: At time chanyu aware it, left, Han army all no merit.

units.zh: 其後四歲，廣以衛尉為將軍，出鴈門擊匈奴。
units.en: Four years later, Guang, in his capacity as Commander of the Palace Guard, was given command of an army and marched out from Yanmen to attack the Xiongnu.
units.literal: Its after four years, Guang with guard wei became general, out Yanmen attacked Xiongnu.

units.zh: 匈奴兵多，破敗廣軍，生得廣。
units.en: The Xiongnu, vastly outnumbering him, routed his army and took Guang alive.
units.literal: Xiongnu troops many, broke defeated Guang army, alive captured Guang.

units.zh: 單于素聞廣賢，令曰：「得李廣必生致之。」
units.en: The Chanyu had long heard that Guang was a man of worth and ordered, "If you capture Li Guang, you must bring him in alive."
units.literal: The Chanyu had long heard that Guang was worthy and ordered, "If you capture Li Guang, you must bring him in alive."

units.zh: 胡騎得廣，廣時傷病，置廣兩馬閒，絡而盛臥廣。
units.en: When the barbarian cavalry seized Guang, he was wounded and ill. They slung a rope net between two horses and laid Guang in it.
units.literal: Hu cavalry got Guang, Guang at time injured ill, placed Guang two horses between, netted and wrapped lay Guang.

units.zh: 行十餘里，廣詳死，睨其旁有一胡兒騎善馬，廣暫騰而上胡兒馬，因推墮兒，取其弓，鞭馬南馳數十里，復得其餘軍，因引而入塞。
units.en: After they had traveled some ten li, Guang feigned death. Glancing to the side, he spotted a barbarian boy riding a fine horse. In a flash, Guang sprang onto the boy's horse, shoved the boy off, seized his bow, and whipped the horse southward. After galloping for several tens of li, he rejoined the remnants of his army and led them back through the frontier pass.
units.literal: Walked ten remainder li, Guang pretended dead, glanced his side had one Hu boy rode good horse, Guang temporarily sprang ascended Hu boy horse, because pushed fell boy, took his bow, whipped horse south galloped several ten li, again got his remaining army, because led entered pass.

units.zh: 匈奴捕者騎數百追之，廣行取胡兒弓，射殺追騎，以故得脫。
units.en: Several hundred Xiongnu horsemen gave chase, but Guang used the barbarian boy's bow to shoot and kill his pursuers, and so made his escape.
units.literal: Xiongnu catchers several hundred pursued him, Guang walking took Hu boy bow, shot killed pursuing cavalry, therefore got escape.

units.zh: 於是至漢，漢下廣吏。
units.en: When he returned to Han territory, he was turned over to the judicial officials.
units.literal: Thereupon arrived Han, Han sent Guang to officials.

units.zh: 吏當廣所失亡多，為虜所生得，當斬，贖為庶人。
units.en: The officials judged that Guang had lost too many men and had been captured alive by the enemy, crimes punishable by death. He was allowed to ransom himself and was reduced to the status of a commoner.
units.literal: Officials judged Guang what lost perished many, by enemy alive captured, should behead, redeemed as commoner.

units.zh: 頃之，家居數歲。
units.en: Before long, he retired to his home, where he lived for some years.
units.literal: Short time, resided home several years.

units.zh: 廣家與故潁陰侯孫屏野居藍田南山中射獵。
units.en: Guang lived with a grandson of the former Marquis of Yingyin in the mountains south of Lantian, where they went hunting.
units.literal: Guang's household lived in seclusion with a grandson of the former Marquis of Yingyin in the mountains south of Lantian, where they went hunting.

units.zh: 嘗夜從一騎出，從人田間飲。
units.en: One night, he rode out with a single companion and drank with some people in the fields.
units.literal: Once night from one cavalry out, followed people field between drank.

units.zh: 還至霸陵亭，霸陵尉醉，呵止廣。
units.en: On the way back, when they reached the Baling postal station, the duty officer, who was drunk, shouted at Guang to halt.
units.literal: Returned to Baling pavilion, Baling wei drunk, shouted stopped Guang.

units.zh: 廣騎曰：「故李將軍。」
units.en: Guang's companion said, "It is the former General Li."
units.literal: Guang's rider said, "The former General Li."

units.zh: 尉曰：「今將軍尚不得夜行，何乃故也！」
units.en: The commandant said, "Even a current general may not travel at night. How much less an old one!"
units.literal: The duty officer said, "Even a serving general may not travel by night—how much less a former one!"

units.zh: 止廣宿亭下。
units.en: He detained Guang and made him spend the night at the station.
units.literal: Stopped Guang stayed pavilion below.

units.zh: 居無何，匈奴入殺遼西太守，敗韓將軍，後韓將軍徙右北平。
units.en: Not long afterward, the Xiongnu invaded and killed the Governor of Liaoxi, defeated General Han Anguo, and Han Anguo was transferred to Youbeiping.
units.literal: Resided no long, Xiongnu entered killed Liaoxi governor, defeated Han general, after Han general moved right Beiping.

units.zh: 於是天子乃召拜廣為右北平太守。
units.en: The Emperor thereupon summoned Guang and appointed him Governor of Youbeiping.
units.literal: Thereupon emperor then summoned appointed Guang as right Beiping governor.

units.zh: 廣即請霸陵尉與俱，至軍而斬之。
units.en: Guang immediately requested that the Baling duty officer accompany him to his post, and upon reaching the army, had the man beheaded.
units.literal: Guang immediately requested Baling wei with together go, arrived army and beheaded him.

units.zh: 廣居右北平，匈奴聞之，號曰「漢之飛將軍」，避之數歲，不敢入右北平。
units.en: While Guang was stationed at Youbeiping, the Xiongnu heard of him, called him "the Flying General of Han," and for several years avoided the region, not daring to enter Youbeiping.
units.literal: While Guang was stationed at Youbeiping, the Xiongnu heard of it, called him "the Flying General of Han," and for several years avoided him, not daring to enter Youbeiping.

units.zh: 廣出獵，見草中石，以為虎而射之，中石沒鏃，視之石也。
units.en: Once, when Guang was out hunting, he saw a rock among the grass and, mistaking it for a tiger, shot at it. The arrow struck the rock and sank in up to the arrowhead. When he looked more closely, he saw it was only a stone.
units.literal: Guang out hunted, saw grass middle stone, considered tiger and shot it, hit stone buried arrowhead, looked it stone.

units.zh: 因復更射之，終不能復入石矣。
units.en: He shot at it again, but could never again make an arrow penetrate the stone.
units.literal: Because again moreover shot it, finally not able again enter stone.

units.zh: 廣所居郡聞有虎，嘗自射之。
units.en: Whenever a tiger was reported in the commandery where Guang was stationed, he would always go out to hunt it himself.
units.literal: Guang what resided commandery heard had tiger, often self shot it.

units.zh: 及居右北平射虎，虎騰傷廣，廣亦竟射殺之。
units.en: While stationed at Youbeiping, he went out to shoot a tiger. The tiger sprang at him and wounded him, but Guang managed to shoot and kill it.
units.literal: When resided right Beiping shot tiger, tiger sprang injured Guang, Guang also finally shot killed it.

units.zh: 廣廉，得賞賜輒分其麾下，飲食與士共之。
units.en: Guang was a man without avarice. Whenever he received a reward or gift, he distributed it among his men, and he shared his food and drink with his soldiers.
units.literal: Guang incorrupt, got reward granted then distributed his command below, drank ate with soldiers shared.

units.zh: 終廣之身，為二千石四十餘年，家無餘財，終不言家產事。
units.en: Throughout his life, Guang held a salary rank of two thousand shi for over forty years, yet his household had no surplus wealth. He never spoke of family property.
units.literal: Finally Guang lifetime, as two thousand shi forty remainder years, home without surplus wealth, finally not spoke home property matters.

units.zh: 廣為人長，猨臂，其善射亦天性也，雖其子孫他人學者，莫能及廣。
units.en: Guang was tall, with unusually long arms like those of an ape. His skill in archery was a gift of nature, and though his sons, grandsons, and others studied the art, none could equal him.
units.literal: Guang as person tall, ape arms, his good shooting also natural talent, though his sons grandsons other people learned, none able match Guang.

units.zh: 廣訥口少言，與人居則畫地為軍陳，射闊狹以飲。
units.en: Guang was a man of few words. When he was with others, he would draw diagrams of battle formations on the ground, and then set up archery contests to determine who would drink, making the targets wider or narrower.
units.literal: Guang slow mouth few words, with people resided then drew ground as army array, shot wide narrow to drink.

units.zh: 專以射為戲，竟死。
units.en: Archery was his sole pastime, and it remained so until the day he died.
units.literal: Specialized with shooting as game, finally died.

units.zh: 廣之將兵，乏絕之處，見水，士卒不盡飲，廣不近水，士卒不盡食，廣不嘗食。
units.en: When Guang led his troops through desolate country and came upon water, he would not go near it until every soldier had drunk his fill. He would not touch his food until every soldier had eaten.
units.literal: Guang led troops, exhausted places, saw water, soldiers not all drank, Guang not approached water, soldiers not all ate, Guang not tasted food.

units.zh: 寬緩不苛，士以此愛樂為用。
units.en: He was lenient and easygoing, never harsh, and for this his soldiers loved him and served him gladly.
units.literal: Lenient relaxed not harsh, soldiers with this loved happy for use.

units.zh: 其射，見敵急，非在數十步之內，度不中不發，發即應弦而倒。
units.en: When he shot at the enemy, he would not release an arrow unless his target was within a few dozen paces, and he was certain of hitting it. When he did let fly, the target fell the instant the bowstring sang.
units.literal: His shooting, saw enemy urgent, not in several ten steps within, measured not hit not fired, fired then responded string fell.

units.zh: 用此，其將兵數困辱，其射猛獸亦為所傷云。
units.en: Because of this habit of closing to short range, he was on several occasions trapped and hard-pressed when leading troops, and when hunting fierce beasts he was sometimes wounded by them as well.
units.literal: Used this, his led troops repeatedly trapped humiliated, his shot fierce beasts also by injured they say.

units.zh: 居頃之，石建卒，於是上召廣代建為郎中令。
units.en: Shortly afterward, Shi Jian died, and the Emperor summoned Guang to replace him as Superintendent of the Imperial Household.
units.literal: Resided short time, Shi Jian died, thereupon emperor summoned Guang replaced Jian became palace secretary.

units.zh: 元朔六年，廣復為後將軍，從大將軍軍出定襄，擊匈奴。
units.en: In the sixth year of the Yuanshuo era, Guang was again appointed General of the Rear and followed the Grand General's army out of Dingxiang to attack the Xiongnu.
units.literal: The sixth year of Yuanshuo, Guang again became rear general, followed grand general army out Dingxiang, attacked Xiongnu.

units.zh: 諸將多中首虜率，以功為侯者，而廣軍無功。
units.en: Many of the other generals met the required kill quotas and were enfeoffed as marquises for their achievements, but Guang's forces earned no distinction.
units.literal: Various generals many hit enemy leaders rates, with merit became marquises, but Guang army no merit.

units.zh: 後二歲，廣以郎中令將四千騎出右北平，博望侯張騫將萬騎與廣俱，異道。
units.en: Two years later, Guang, in his capacity as Superintendent of the Imperial Household, led four thousand cavalry out of Youbeiping. The Marquis of Bowang, Zhang Qian, led ten thousand cavalry on a parallel route.
units.literal: After two years, Guang with palace secretary led four thousand cavalry out right Beiping, Bowang marquis Zhang Qian led ten thousand cavalry with Guang together, different roads.

units.zh: 行可數百里，匈奴左賢王將四萬騎圍廣，廣軍士皆恐，廣乃使其子敢往馳之。
units.en: After they had advanced several hundred li, the Left Worthy King of the Xiongnu descended upon them with forty thousand cavalry and surrounded Guang. His soldiers were all terrified. Guang sent his son Li Gan to ride out against the enemy.
units.literal: Marched could several hundred li, Xiongnu left worthy king led four ten thousand cavalry surrounded Guang, Guang army soldiers all feared, Guang then sent his son Gan go galloped them.

units.zh: 敢獨與數十騎馳，直貫胡騎，出其左右而還，告廣曰：「胡虜易與耳。」
units.en: Gan rode out alone with several dozen horsemen, charged straight through the barbarian cavalry, emerged on their flanks, and returned. He reported to Guang, "The Hu cavalry are easy to handle."
units.literal: Gan rode out alone with several dozen horsemen, charged straight through the barbarian cavalry, broke out to their left and right, and returned. He reported to Guang, saying, "The barbarian enemy are easy to deal with."

units.zh: 軍士乃安。
units.en: Only then did the soldiers' courage steady.
units.literal: Army soldiers then calm.

units.zh: 廣為圜陳外向，胡急擊之，矢下如雨。
units.en: Guang formed his men into a circular formation facing outward. The barbarians attacked furiously, and arrows fell like rain.
units.literal: Guang made circular array outward facing, Hu urgently attacked it, arrows fell like rain.

units.zh: 漢兵死者過半，漢矢且盡。
units.en: More than half the Han soldiers were killed, and their arrows were nearly exhausted.
units.literal: Han troops died over half, Han arrows almost exhausted.

units.zh: 廣乃令士持滿毋發，而廣身自以大黃射其裨將，殺數人，胡虜益解。
units.en: Guang ordered his soldiers to draw their bows fully but hold their fire, while he himself took up a powerful crossbow and shot at the enemy's deputy commanders, killing several. The barbarian assault gradually slackened.
units.literal: Guang then ordered soldiers hold full not fire, and Guang personally with big yellow shot their deputy generals, killed several people, Hu enemy increasingly loosened.

units.zh: 會日暮，吏士皆無人色，而廣意氣自如，益治軍。
units.en: As dusk fell, every officer and soldier had gone pale with fear, but Guang remained as composed as ever, rallying his troops with ever greater resolve.
units.literal: Met dusk, officers soldiers all without human color, but Guang spirit energy self like, increasingly governed army.

units.zh: 軍中自是服其勇也。
units.en: From that time on, every man in the army admired his courage.
units.literal: Army middle from this submitted his courage.

units.zh: 明日，復力戰，而博望侯軍亦至，匈奴軍乃解去。
units.en: The next day, they fought on fiercely, and the army of the Marquis of Bowang arrived at last. The Xiongnu withdrew.
units.literal: Next day, again vigorously fought, and Bowang marquis army also arrived, Xiongnu army then withdrew left.

units.zh: 漢軍罷，弗能追。
units.en: The Han army was too exhausted to give chase.
units.literal: Han army dismissed, not able pursue.

units.zh: 是時廣軍幾沒，罷歸。
units.en: Guang's army had been all but annihilated, and the survivors straggled home.
units.literal: At time Guang army almost perished, dismissed returned.

units.zh: 漢法，博望侯留遲後期，當死，贖為庶人。
units.en: Under Han law, the Marquis of Bowang was charged with arriving late past the appointed rendezvous, a crime punishable by death. He was allowed to ransom himself and was reduced to the status of a commoner.
units.literal: Han law, Bowang marquis stayed late after period, should die, redeemed as commoner.

units.zh: 廣軍功自如，無賞。
units.en: As for Guang, his army's gains and losses canceled each other out, and he received no reward.
units.literal: Guang army merit self like, no reward.

units.zh: 初，廣之從弟李蔡與廣俱事孝文帝。
units.en: Earlier, Guang's younger cousin Li Cai had entered service alongside Guang under Emperor Wen.
units.literal: Initially, Guang younger cousin Li Cai with Guang together served Emperor Wen.

units.zh: 景帝時，蔡積功勞至二千石。
units.en: Under Emperor Jing, Cai had accumulated enough merit to attain the rank of two thousand shi.
units.literal: Emperor Jing time, Cai accumulated merit labor to two thousand shi.

units.zh: 孝武帝時，至代相。
units.en: Under Emperor Wu, he rose to become Chancellor of Dai.
units.literal: Emperor Wu time, to Dai chancellor.

units.zh: 以元朔五年為輕車將車，從大將軍擊右賢王，有功中率，封為樂安侯。
units.en: In the fifth year of the Yuanshuo era, he served as General of the Light Chariots and followed the Grand General in an attack on the Right Worthy King. He met the required kill quota and was enfeoffed as the Marquis of Le'an.
units.literal: With the fifth year of Yuanshuo became light chariot general, followed grand general attacked right worthy king, had merit hit rate, sealed as Lean hou.

units.zh: 元狩二年中，代公孫弘為丞相。
units.en: In the second year of the Yuanshou era, he succeeded Gongsun Hong as Imperial Chancellor.
units.literal: The second year of Yuanshou middle, replaced Gongsun Hong became chancellor.

units.zh: 蔡為人在下中，名聲出廣下甚遠，然廣不得爵邑，官不過九卿，而蔡為列侯，位至三公。
units.en: Cai was a man of middling ability at best, and his reputation fell far below Guang's. Yet Guang never received a noble title or a fief, and his office never rose above that of one of the Nine Ministers, while Cai became a full marquis and attained the rank of one of the Three Excellencies.
units.literal: Cai as person in lower middle, fame reputation out Guang below very far, but Guang not got nobility fief, office not passed nine ministers, but Cai became marquises, position to three dukes.

units.zh: 諸廣之軍吏及士卒或取封侯。
units.en: Even officers and soldiers who had served under Guang were among those enfeoffed as marquises.
units.literal: Various Guang army officers and soldiers or took sealed marquises.

units.zh: 廣嘗與望氣王朔燕語，曰：「自漢擊匈奴而廣未嘗不在其中，而諸部校尉以下，才能不及中人，然以擊胡軍功取侯者數十人，而廣不為後人，然無尺寸之功以得封邑者，何也？
units.en: Guang once conversed at leisure with the diviner Wang Shuo and said, "Since the Han began attacking the Xiongnu, I have never failed to be in the field. Yet among the colonels and commanders and those below them, men whose abilities do not reach the middling level have, through merit in fighting the barbarians, become marquises by the dozens. I am not behind others, yet I have not the slightest merit by which to receive a fief—why is this?
units.literal: Guang once conversed at leisure with the diviner Wang Shuo and said, "Since the Han began attacking the Xiongnu, I have never failed to be among them. Yet among the colonels and commanders and those below them, men whose abilities do not reach the middling level have, through merit in fighting the barbarians, become marquises by the dozens. I am not behind others, yet I have not the slightest merit by which to receive a fief—why is this?

units.zh: 豈吾相不當侯邪？
units.en: Can it be that my features are not those of a man destined for a marquisate?
units.literal: Is it that my physiognomy is not suited to be a marquis?

units.zh: 且固命也？」
units.en: Or is it simply fate?"
units.literal: Or is it simply fate?"

units.zh: 朔曰：「將軍自念，豈嘗有所恨乎？」
units.en: Shuo said, "General, think back for yourself. Is there anything you have regretted?"
units.literal: Shuo said, "General, reflect for yourself—have you ever had something you regret?"

units.zh: 廣曰：「吾嘗為隴西守，羌嘗反，吾誘而降，降者八百餘人，吾詐而同日殺之。
units.en: Guang said, "I once served as Governor of Longxi. When the Qiang rebelled, I enticed them into surrender; more than eight hundred surrendered, and I deceived them and killed them all on the same day.
units.literal: Guang said, "I once served as Governor of Longxi. When the Qiang rebelled, I lured them to surrender; more than eight hundred who surrendered I deceived and killed on the same day.

units.zh: 至今大恨獨此耳。」
units.en: To this day, that alone is my deepest regret."
units.literal: To this day my greatest regret is this alone."

units.zh: 朔曰：「禍莫大於殺已降，此乃將軍所以不得侯者也。」
units.en: Shuo said, "There is no greater disaster than killing men who have already surrendered. This is why the general has never become a marquis."
units.literal: Shuo said, "No calamity is greater than killing men who have already surrendered—this is why the general has not become a marquis."

units.zh: 後二歲，大將軍、驃騎將軍大出擊匈奴，廣數自請行。
units.en: Two years later, the Grand General and the General of the Swift Cavalry launched a major campaign against the Xiongnu. Guang repeatedly petitioned to join them.
units.literal: After two years, grand general, flying cavalry general greatly out attacked Xiongnu, Guang repeatedly self requested go.

units.zh: 天子以為老，弗許；
units.en: The emperor thought him too old and would not allow it;
units.literal: The emperor considered him too old and did not permit it;

units.zh: 良久乃許之，以為前將軍。
units.en: After a long delay, the Emperor relented and appointed him General of the Vanguard.
units.literal: Long time then permitted him, appointed as front general.

units.zh: 是歲，元狩四年也。
units.en: This was the fourth year of the Yuanshou era.
units.literal: This year, the fourth year of Yuanshou.

units.zh: 廣既從大將軍青擊匈奴，既出塞，青捕虜知單于所居，乃自以精兵走之，而令廣并於右將軍軍，出東道。
units.en: Guang marched with Grand General Wei Qing to attack the Xiongnu. After they had crossed the frontier, Qing learned from captured prisoners where the Chanyu was camped. He took his best troops to go after the Chanyu himself and ordered Guang to merge his forces with the General of the Right and advance by the eastern route.
units.literal: Guang already followed grand general Qing attacked Xiongnu, already out pass, Qing captured captives knew chanyu residence, then self with elite troops went it, and ordered Guang merged with right general army, out east road.

units.zh: 東道少回遠，而大軍行水草少，其勢不屯行。
units.en: The eastern route was circuitous and far, with little water or grass along the way, making it difficult for a large force to march and encamp.
units.literal: East road few winding distant, but main army marched water grass few, its situation not garrison march.

units.zh: 廣自請曰：「臣部為前將軍，今大將軍乃徙令臣出東道，且臣結發而與匈奴戰，今乃一得當單于，臣願居前，先死單于。」
units.en: Guang pleaded on his own behalf, saying, "My command is the Vanguard. Now the Grand General has shifted me to the eastern route. I have fought the Xiongnu since I first bound up my hair, and now, for once, I have the chance to face the Chanyu. I wish to stand in the front and be the first to die before him."
units.literal: Guang petitioned on his own behalf, saying, "My command is that of General of the Vanguard. Now the Grand General has reassigned me to the eastern route. Moreover, I have fought the Xiongnu since I first bound up my hair. Now at last I have a chance to face the Chanyu—I wish to take the front rank and be the first to meet the Chanyu in death."

units.zh: 大將軍青亦陰受上誡，以為李廣老，數奇，毋令當單于，恐不得所欲。
units.en: Grand General Qing had also received secret instructions from the Emperor: Li Guang was old and had always been unlucky; he must not be allowed to face the Chanyu, for fear that the desired result would not be achieved.
units.literal: Grand general Qing also secretly received emperor instruction, considered Li Guang old, repeatedly unlucky, not let face chanyu, feared not get desired.

units.zh: 而是時公孫敖新失侯，為中將軍從大將軍，大將軍亦欲使敖與俱當單于，故徙前將軍廣。
units.en: Moreover, Gongsun Ao had recently lost his marquisate and was serving as General of the Center under the Grand General. The Grand General wished to give Ao the chance to face the Chanyu alongside him, and so he reassigned Guang from the vanguard.
units.literal: And at time Gongsun Ao newly lost marquis, became middle general followed grand general, grand general also wanted make Ao with together face chanyu, therefore moved front general Guang.

units.zh: 廣時知之，固自辭於大將軍。
units.en: Guang understood what was happening and firmly protested to the Grand General.
units.literal: Guang at time knew it, firmly self declined with grand general.

units.zh: 大將軍不聽，令長史封書與廣之莫府，曰：「急詣部，如書。」
units.en: The Grand General would not listen. He ordered the chief clerk to seal a letter to Guang’s headquarters, saying, "Report at once to the command assigned in the letter."
units.literal: The Grand General would not listen. He had the chief clerk seal a letter to Guang's headquarters, saying, "Proceed at once to your command as written."

units.zh: 廣不謝大將軍而起行，意甚慍怒而就部，引兵與右將軍食其合軍出東道。
units.en: Guang departed without taking leave of the Grand General, seething with resentment. He went to take up his command and led his troops eastward with the General of the Right, Zhao Shiqi.
units.literal: Guang not thanked grand general and rose marched, intent very resentful angered and went command, led troops with right general Shiqi combined army out east road.

units.zh: 軍亡導，或失道，後大將軍。
units.en: The army had no guide and lost its way, falling behind the Grand General's schedule.
units.literal: Army lacked guide, or lost road, after grand general.

units.zh: 大將軍與單于接戰，單于遁走，弗能得而還。
units.en: The Grand General engaged the Chanyu in battle, but the Chanyu escaped and could not be captured, so the Grand General turned back.
units.literal: Grand general with chanyu engaged battle, chanyu fled ran, not able get and returned.

units.zh: 南絕幕，遇前將軍、右將軍。
units.en: As he crossed south through the desert, he encountered the General of the Vanguard and the General of the Right.
units.literal: South cut off tent, met front general, right general.

units.zh: 廣已見大將軍，還入軍。
units.en: After Guang had met with the Grand General, he returned to his own camp.
units.literal: Guang already saw grand general, returned entered army.

units.zh: 大將軍使長史持糒醪遺廣，因問廣、食其失道狀，青欲上書報天子軍曲折。
units.en: The Grand General sent his chief clerk to bring Guang dried rations and wine, and at the same time to question Guang and Zhao Shiqi about how they had lost their way, for Qing wished to submit a report to the Emperor on the course of the campaign.
units.literal: Grand general sent chancellor secretary held dried grains wine gifted Guang, because asked Guang, Shiqi lost road condition, Qing wanted memorial reported emperor army twists turns.

units.zh: 廣未對，大將軍使長史急責廣之幕府對簿。
units.en: Guang made no reply. The Grand General then sent his chief clerk to summon Guang urgently to headquarters to answer formal charges.
units.literal: Guang not responded, grand general sent chancellor secretary urgently blamed Guang headquarters respond trial.

units.zh: 廣曰：「諸校尉無罪，乃我自失道。
units.en: Guang said, "The colonels are not at fault. I myself lost the road.
units.literal: Guang said, "The colonels are not guilty—it was I who lost the way.

units.zh: 吾今自上簿。」
units.en: I will now present myself and answer for it."
units.literal: I will now go up and answer the charges myself."

units.zh: 至莫府，廣謂其麾下曰；
units.en: When Guang reached headquarters, he said to the officers under him,
units.literal: When he reached headquarters, Guang said to his officers,

units.zh: 「廣結發與匈奴大小七十餘戰，今幸從大將軍出接單于兵，而大將軍又徙廣部行回遠，而又迷失道，豈非天哉！
units.en: "Since I first bound up my hair, I have fought the Xiongnu in more than seventy battles, large and small. Now I was fortunate enough to follow the Grand General out to meet the Chanyu’s army, but the Grand General shifted my command onto a roundabout and distant route, and then we lost the way. Is this not Heaven!
units.literal: "Since I first bound up my hair I have fought the Xiongnu in great and small engagements more than seventy times. Now, having had the good fortune to follow the Grand General out against the Chanyu's army, the Grand General has again reassigned my command to the winding eastern route, and moreover we lost our way—is this not Heaven's will!

units.zh: 且廣年六十餘矣，終不能復對刀筆之吏。」
units.en: Moreover, I am already more than sixty years old; I can no longer face the sword-and-brush officials."
units.literal: Moreover, Guang is already more than sixty years old; I can no longer face the sword-and-brush officials."

units.zh: 遂引刀自剄。
units.en: With that, he drew his sword and cut his own throat.
units.literal: Then drew knife self cut throat.

units.zh: 廣軍士大夫一軍皆哭。
units.en: The officers and men of Guang's entire army wept.
units.literal: Guang army scholar officials one army all cried.

units.zh: 百姓聞之，知與不知，無老壯皆為垂涕。
units.en: When the common people heard the news, whether they had known him or not, old and young alike shed tears for him.
units.literal: Common people heard it, knew and not knew, without old strong all for hung tears.

units.zh: 而右將軍獨下吏，當死，贖為庶人。
units.en: As for the General of the Right, he alone was turned over to the judicial officials. Found guilty of a capital offense, he ransomed himself and was reduced to the status of a commoner.
units.literal: But right general alone sent officials, should die, redeemed as commoner.

units.zh: 廣子三人，曰當戶、椒、敢，為郎。
units.en: Guang had three sons, named Danghu, Jiao, and Gan, all of whom served as Imperial Attendants.
units.literal: Guang sons three people, named Danghu, Jiao, Gan, became imperial attendants.

units.zh: 天子與韓嫣戲，嫣少不遜，當戶擊嫣，嫣走。
units.en: Once, when the Emperor was amusing himself with his favorite Han Yan, Yan behaved disrespectfully. Danghu struck Yan, who fled.
units.literal: Emperor with Han Yan played, Yan young not respectful, Danghu hit Yan, Yan fled.

units.zh: 於是天子以為勇。
units.en: The Emperor regarded Danghu as a man of courage for this.
units.literal: Thereupon emperor considered brave.

units.zh: 當戶早死，拜椒為代郡太守，皆先廣死。
units.en: Danghu died young. Jiao was appointed Governor of Dai Commandery. Both sons died before their father.
units.literal: Danghu early died, appointed Jiao as Daijun governor, all before Guang died.

units.zh: 當戶有遺腹子名陵。
units.en: Danghu left behind a posthumous son named Li Ling.
units.literal: Danghu had posthumous son named Ling.

units.zh: 廣死軍時，敢從驃騎將軍。
units.en: At the time of Guang's death in the field, his son Gan was serving under the General of the Swift Cavalry.
units.literal: Guang died army time, Gan followed flying cavalry general.

units.zh: 廣死明年，李蔡以丞相坐侵孝景園壖地，當下吏治，蔡亦自殺，不對獄，國除。
units.en: The year after Guang died, Li Cai, then serving as Imperial Chancellor, was charged with encroaching on the land around Emperor Jing's funerary park. Facing prosecution, Cai too took his own life rather than submit to interrogation, and his fief was abolished.
units.literal: Guang died next year, Li Cai with chancellor sat encroached Emperor Jing garden wall land, should sent officials treated, Cai also suicide, not responded prison, fief removed.

units.zh: 李敢以校尉從驃騎將軍擊胡左賢王，力戰，奪左賢王鼓旗，斬首多，賜爵關內侯，食邑二百戶，代廣為郎中令。
units.en: Li Gan, serving as a colonel under the General of the Swift Cavalry, had fought valiantly against the Left Worthy King of the Xiongnu, seizing the enemy's war drums and battle standards and taking many heads. He was granted the title of Marquis Within the Passes with a fief of two hundred households, and succeeded his father as Superintendent of the Imperial Household.
units.literal: Li Gan with colonel followed flying cavalry general attacked Hu left worthy king, vigorously fought, took left worthy king drum flags, beheaded heads many, granted nobility Guannei hou, ate fief two hundred households, replaced Guang became palace secretary.

units.zh: 頃之，怨大將軍青之恨其父，乃擊傷大將軍，大將軍匿諱之。
units.en: Before long, Gan, harboring resentment against Grand General Qing for having driven his father to his death, attacked and wounded the Grand General. The Grand General concealed the incident.
units.literal: Short time, resented grand general Qing hated his father, then hit injured grand general, grand general hid covered it.

units.zh: 居無何，敢從上雍，至甘泉宮獵。
units.en: Not long afterward, Gan accompanied the Emperor on a journey to Yong and went hunting at the Ganquan Palace.
units.literal: Resided no long, Gan followed emperor Yong, arrived Ganquan palace hunted.

units.zh: 驃騎將軍去病與青有親，射殺敢。
units.en: The General of the Swift Cavalry, Huo Qubing, who was related to Wei Qing, shot and killed Gan.
units.literal: Flying cavalry general Huo Qubing with Qing had relation, shot killed Gan.

units.zh: 去病時方貴幸，上諱云鹿觸殺之。
units.en: Huo Qubing was at the height of imperial favor at the time, and the Emperor covered up the deed, declaring that Gan had been killed by a charging deer.
units.literal: Qubing at time just noble favored, emperor hid said deer bumped killed him.

units.zh: 居歲餘，去病死。
units.en: A little more than a year later, Huo Qubing died.
units.literal: Resided year remainder, Qubing died.

units.zh: 而敢有女為太子中人，愛幸，敢男禹有寵於太子，然好利，李氏陵遲衰微矣。
units.en: Gan had a daughter who served in the Crown Prince's household and was favored by him. Gan's son Li Yu also enjoyed the Crown Prince's patronage, but he was a man who cared only for profit, and the Li family gradually declined.
units.literal: But Gan had a daughter who was a palace woman of the Crown Prince and was favored; Gan's son Yu had favor with the Crown Prince, but liked profit, and the Li clan gradually declined and weakened.

units.zh: 李陵既壯，選為建章監，監諸騎。
units.en: When Li Ling came of age, he was selected to serve as Superintendent of the Jianzhang Palace, in charge of the cavalry.
units.literal: Li Ling already grown, selected became Jianzhang monitor, monitored various cavalry.

units.zh: 善射，愛士卒。
units.en: He was a skilled archer who treated his soldiers with care.
units.literal: Good shooting, loved soldiers.

units.zh: 天子以為李氏世將，而使將八百騎。
units.en: The Emperor, considering the Li family a line of hereditary generals, gave him command of eight hundred cavalry.
units.literal: Emperor considered Li clan world generals, and made lead eight hundred cavalry.

units.zh: 嘗深入匈奴二千餘里，過居延視地形，無所見虜而還。
units.en: He once penetrated more than two thousand li into Xiongnu territory, passing through Juyan to survey the terrain, but encountered no enemy and returned.
units.literal: Once deeply entered Xiongnu two thousand remainder li, passed Juyan viewed terrain, nothing saw enemy returned.

units.zh: 拜為騎都尉，將丹陽楚人五千人，教射酒泉、張掖以屯衛胡。
units.en: He was appointed Commandant of Cavalry and given command of five thousand men from Danyang and Chu, whom he trained in archery at Jiuquan and Zhangye to garrison the frontier against the barbarians.
units.literal: Appointed became cavalry commandery governor, led Danyang Chu people five thousand people, taught shooting Jiuquan, Zhangye to garrison guard Hu.

units.zh: 數歲，天漢二年秋，貳師將軍李廣利將三萬騎擊匈奴右賢王於祁連天山，而使陵將其射士步兵五千人出居延北可千餘里，欲以分匈奴兵，毋令專走貳師也。
units.en: Several years later, in the autumn of the second year of the Tianhan era, General Li Guangli of Ershi led thirty thousand cavalry to attack the Right Worthy King of the Xiongnu in the Qilian and Tianshan mountains. Li Ling was ordered to lead his five thousand archers and infantry north from Juyan, about a thousand li deep, to draw off part of the Xiongnu forces and prevent them from concentrating against Li Guangli.
units.literal: Several years, Tianhan second year autumn, Ershi general Li Guangli led three ten thousand cavalry attacked Xiongnu right worthy king at Qilian Tianshan, and made Ling lead his archers infantry five thousand people out Juyan north could thousand remainder li, wanted with divide Xiongnu troops, not let specialize run Ershi.

units.zh: 陵既至期還，而單于以兵八萬圍擊陵軍。
units.en: When Ling had reached the appointed rendezvous and was turning back, the Chanyu descended upon him with eighty thousand men and surrounded his army.
units.literal: Ling already arrived period returned, but chanyu with troops eight ten thousand surrounded attacked Ling army.

units.zh: 陵軍五千人，兵矢既盡，士死者過半，而所殺傷匈奴亦萬餘人。
units.en: Ling's army of five thousand fought until their weapons and arrows were exhausted. More than half his men were killed, but they had also killed or wounded more than ten thousand of the Xiongnu.
units.literal: Ling army five thousand people, troops arrows already exhausted, soldiers died over half, and what killed wounded Xiongnu also ten thousand remainder people.

units.zh: 且引且戰，連鬬八日，還未到居延百餘里，匈奴遮狹絕道，陵食乏而救兵不到，虜急擊招降陵。
units.en: Fighting as they retreated, they battled for eight days straight. When they were still more than a hundred li from Juyan, the Xiongnu blocked the narrow passes and cut off their route. Ling's provisions were spent and no reinforcements came. The enemy pressed their attack and called on Ling to surrender.
units.literal: Pulling led fighting, continuously battled eight days, returned not arrived Juyan hundred remainder li, Xiongnu blocked narrow cut off road, Ling food exhausted and rescue troops not arrived, enemy urgently attacked summoned surrender Ling.

units.zh: 陵曰：「無面目報陛下。」
units.en: Ling said, "I have no face with which to report back to Your Majesty."
units.literal: Ling said, "I have no face with which to report to Your Majesty."

units.zh: 遂降匈奴。
units.en: And so he surrendered to the Xiongnu.
units.literal: Then surrendered Xiongnu.

units.zh: 其兵盡沒，餘亡散得歸漢者四百餘人。
units.en: His forces were destroyed. Of the survivors who fled and scattered, only some four hundred managed to make their way back to Han territory.
units.literal: His troops all perished, remaining fled scattered got return Han four hundred remainder people.

units.zh: 單于既得陵，素聞其家聲，及戰又壯，乃以其女妻陵而貴之。
units.en: After the Chanyu had taken Ling captive, he had long heard of the Li family's reputation, and Ling had fought with great valor. He therefore gave Ling one of his own daughters in marriage and honored him.
units.literal: Chanyu already got Ling, long heard his family reputation, and battle moreover brave, then with his daughter married Ling and honored him.

units.zh: 漢聞，族陵母妻子。
units.en: When the Han court learned of this, it had Ling's mother, wife, and children executed.
units.literal: Han heard, executed Ling mother wife children.

units.zh: 自是之後，李氏名敗，而隴西之士居門下者皆用為恥焉。
units.en: From that time on, the name of the Li family was disgraced, and the men of Longxi who had once been proud to call themselves their retainers now felt only shame.
units.literal: From this after, Li clan name failed, but Longxi scholars resided gate below all used as shame.

units.zh: 太史公曰：傳曰：「其身正，不令而行；
units.en: The Grand Historian says: The tradition says, "When a man’s own conduct is upright, things are done even without commands;
units.literal: The Grand Historian says: The tradition says, "When his person is upright, he need not command and his orders are carried out;

units.zh: 其身不正，雖令不從。」
units.en: when his own conduct is not upright, even commands are not obeyed."
units.literal: when his person is not upright, though he commands, they are not obeyed."

units.zh: 其李將軍之謂也？
units.en: Was this not said of General Li?
units.literal: Is this not what is meant by General Li?

units.zh: 余睹李將軍悛悛如鄙人，口不能道辭。
units.en: I once saw General Li in person. He was as plain and unassuming as a common farmer, and he could scarcely string two words together.
units.literal: I observed Li general honest like common person, mouth not able speak words.

units.zh: 及死之日，天下知與不知，皆為盡哀。
units.en: Yet on the day of his death, everyone in the realm, whether they had known him or not, grieved for him with all their hearts.
units.literal: When died day, realm knew and not knew, all for exhausted sorrow.

units.zh: 彼其忠實心誠信於士大夫也？
units.en: Was it because his faithful and sincere heart was trusted by the scholar-officials?
units.literal: Was it because his loyal and sincere heart won the trust of the scholar-officials?

units.zh: 諺曰「桃李不言，下自成蹊」。
units.en: A proverb says, "Peach and plum trees do not speak, yet beneath them a path forms of itself."
units.literal: A proverb says, "Peach and plum trees do not speak, yet a path is worn beneath them."

units.zh: 此言雖小，可以諭大也。
units.en: This saying may seem a small thing, but it speaks to something great.
units.literal: This words though small, can illustrate great.
